clue.text: Shame is brought to street by a carnival

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust, as in 'fie for shame'

explanation.surface: Some disgrace comes to a road when a travelling fair rolls in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive holiday or celebration, much like a carnival.

clue.text: One taken in by false Lord, is 'e?

definitions.text: One taken in by false Lord, is 'e?

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the other letters, which take it in
the letters of these words are not genuine in order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a cockney dropping the h of he, leaving the single letter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cockney asks whether someone has been fooled by a sham god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e is cockney for he. Read as a whole, the clue pictures someone duped by a sham god, which is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone duped by a false deity is a worshipper, one who adores an idol.

clue.text: Facilities for kids outdoors, and covered in spells of rain

indicators.note: the word 'and' is enclosed by the rain word, which covers it

parts.note: spits are brief light showers, as in 'it's spitting'

explanation.surface: Children's outdoor play areas get soaked by showers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpits are areas of sand where children play outside.

clue.text: Hazardous operation to make a set of false teeth, about five

indicators.note: the teeth word goes around the numeral, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth, with a for the article
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Making dentures turns out to be a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a bold, risky undertaking.

clue.text: Chap's surrounded by gloomy darkness in foreign port

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed on both sides by the other, so the man's words go inside the darkness

parts.note: murk is thick gloom or darkness
a chap is a man, so chap's gives man's

explanation.surface: A man is lost in the gloom of some port abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmansk is a Russian seaport on the Kola Peninsula, so a port in a foreign country.

clue.text: Good news offered by notes members receive?

definitions.text: Good news offered by notes members receive?

parts.words: Good news offered by notes members receive?
parts.note: welcome news, pictured as tunes made of notes that the hearing organs, parts of the body, take in

explanation.surface: Glad tidings come from musical notes that body parts pick up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' are body parts here: the ears, which receive the notes of a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes news that is very welcome and pleasant to hear.

clue.text: Islander wins game point — it's outside the line

indicators.note: the game word sits on both sides of the line, enclosing it

parts.note: in chess, a player who wins mates the opponent
L is a common abbreviation for line
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone from an island scores at match point, but the ball is called out.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture of a point landing outside the line hides chess: 'wins game' is checkmates.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maltese person is a native of the Mediterranean island of Malta.

clue.text: Worm, harmless, coming up in a knot

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the knot word

parts.note: a node is a knot, as in a tree or a line

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word harmless gives letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a tame animal is harmless

explanation.surface: A harmless worm surfaces tied in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmless' suggests a description of the worm, but it supplies letters; in a down entry 'coming up' reads them upwards (EMAT).
explanation.definitionFit: A nematode is a roundworm, a type of parasitic or free-living worm.

clue.text: Instrument's sound quality provides necessary support

parts.note: a key is an instrument for opening locks, so instrument's gives key's
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: The timbre of a musical instrument gives it essential backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music but is a lock key.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone of an arch that holds it all up, so a vital support.

clue.text: Conspires to perpetrate trick with weapons, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a con is a trick and knives are weapons, so together con and knives

explanation.surface: Someone plots a swindle involving arms, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To connive is to plot or collude secretly, which is what conspirators do.

clue.text: Sticky sort of soil in which French gents may get stuck

indicators.note: the gentlemen become stuck inside the soil, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: clay is a heavy, sticky type of soil
MM is the abbreviation of messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Frenchmen bog down in heavy, gluey earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy means damp and sticky to the touch.

clue.text: The fellow's fear of Spain

parts.note: belonging to that man is 'his'
panic is sudden overwhelming fear

explanation.surface: A man is afraid of the country of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic is the adjective relating to Spain or Spanish-speaking peoples.

clue.text: Two groups (each of three characters) may interlock to form it

definitions.text: Two groups (each of three characters) may interlock to form it

parts.words: Two groups (each of three characters) may interlock to form it
parts.note: two copies of a three-letter word for a group, their letters alternating, spell the answer; and the answer is itself a group of six

explanation.surface: Two trios of letters mesh together to make something.
explanation.walkthrough: Interleave S-E-T with S-E-T, taking a letter from each in turn, and you get S,E,S,T,E,T. A sestet is also two tercets (three-line groups) joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a group of six, especially the last six lines of a sonnet, made of two three-line units.

clue.text: French city trip cut short by mean person

indicators.note: the word for a trip loses its final letter, as if trimmed at the end

parts.note: a tour is a trip
a louse is a contemptible, mean person

explanation.surface: A journey abroad is curtailed by some nasty character.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in southern France.

clue.text: Bird is all neck and beak

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, which is also to spoon
a bill is a bird's beak

explanation.surface: A bird consists entirely of throat and bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' looks like a body part; it is the verb, to canoodle, as is to spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a flat, spoon-shaped bill.

clue.text: King repulsed knight with knife

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: driven back, so the word for a knight is read backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A monarch fends off a mounted warrior armed with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Where Mahdists gained victory bringing terrible harm to UK

indicators.note: the letters of 'harm to UK' are messed up terribly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic defeat for Britain, recalling the fall of Gordon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahdists, Sudanese followers of the Mahdi, captured Khartoum in 1885, killing General Gordon: real harm to the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese capital was taken by Mahdist forces in 1885, their great victory.

clue.text: Maltreatin' without love, giving a false impression

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the maltreating word is wrapped around love

parts.note: to maltreat is to ill-use, so maltreating is ill-using, here with the final g dropped
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Cruelty without affection creates a misleading picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The apostrophe tells you the G of ILL-USING is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is something that deceives the senses or mind, a false impression.

clue.text: Traditional advice found in sacred epistles

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words 'sacred epistles', across the word break

explanation.surface: Time-honoured counsel can be read in the holy letters of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rede is an archaic word for counsel or advice.

clue.text: Second-hand items the retired may have been given?

definitions.text: Second-hand items the retired may have been given?

parts.words: Second-hand items the retired may have been given?
parts.note: read 'retired' as re-tyred, fitted with new tyres, which used tyres with fresh tread would do

explanation.surface: Pensioners might receive cast-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests pensioners, but read it as re-tyred: a vehicle given remoulded tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreads are old tyres given new treads, so reused second-hand goods.

clue.text: Female clergyman may turn out to be a bossy type!

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A woman priest might prove domineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is the one in charge, who tells others what to do.

clue.text: Runner in front? European bod who's tall and thin

indicators.note: the runner comes first, placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a runner is a runner bean, a climbing bean
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: An athlete from Europe at the head of the field is a lanky sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the vegetable: runner beans climb up tall poles, a neat link to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is informal for a very tall, skinny person.

clue.text: Look funny in a sleeping bag

parts.note: to look a certain way is to be that way in appearance
droll means amusing or funny

explanation.surface: Someone seems comical lying in a sleeping bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroll is bedding rolled up for carrying, such as a sleeping bag.

clue.text: Some bread deliverers may make them

definitions.text: Some bread deliverers may make them

parts.words: Some bread deliverers may make them
parts.note: a baker's delivery man goes on a regular circuit, and bread itself is cut into slices of a matching name

explanation.surface: Bakery van drivers might produce these.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two senses here: a delivery circuit, and a slice of bread (a round of toast or sandwiches).
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds are both the routes a delivery person follows and whole slices of bread.

clue.text: Paper takes the moisture out of miscellaneous items

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
removing moisture from something dries it

explanation.surface: A newspaper soaks up the damp from assorted bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are various small items too minor to list separately.

clue.text: Prayer one used in Wells

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the name, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Orson Welles, the film director, though printed here with the spelling of the cathedral city of Wells
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single prayer is said in the cathedral city of Wells, in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the cathedral city in Somerset, apt for a prayer, but it is the American actor-director Orson Welles, punning on the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: Girl embracing six-footer in Spanish port

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps its arms around the insect, so it goes inside

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
an insect such as an ant has six legs

explanation.surface: A young woman hugs a tall man in a harbour town in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Be more easy-going, being stupid

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means care less, become more relaxed; as one word it means thoughtless or foolish.

clue.text: Strong desire by engineers to show brilliance

parts.note: lust is intense desire
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Keen ambition among engineers makes them shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gentle shine or sheen, a kind of brilliance.
